claims.text: The target material is a cast, Ti- and Ni-containing, single-phase high-entropy solid solution that has not received post-synthesis homogenization.
Post-casting high-temperature homogenization will improve the elevated-temperature mechanical performance of the target Ti-Ni-based alloy relative to its non-homogenized state.
Homogenization will reduce compositional inhomogeneities in the target alloy.
Homogenization will suppress precipitates or segregation in the target alloy.
A treatment near 2100°C for a short duration followed by controlled cooling may be suitable for the Ti-Ni-based target alloy.
The relevant elevated-temperature test regime spans approximately 700°C to 1600°C.
Trace interstitials can promote alpha-Ti precipitation during elevated-temperature aging and thereby cause softening.
The proposed homogenization treatment will prevent alpha-Ti or other secondary-phase formation in the target Ti-Ni alloy.
High-temperature treatment promotes atomic diffusion and homogenizes the distribution of constituent elements.
A homogeneous elemental distribution stabilizes the single-phase solid solution in the target Ti-Ni alloy.
Reducing local compositional variations minimizes nucleation of deleterious secondary phases.
Secondary phases or segregated regions can act as stress concentrators at elevated temperature.
The homogenized alloy will have higher elevated-temperature yield strength than the non-homogenized alloy.
The homogenized alloy may have higher elevated-temperature ductility than the non-homogenized alloy.
The homogenized alloy will retain greater mechanical stability during elevated-temperature exposure than the non-homogenized alloy.
The non-homogenized baseline may develop compositional inhomogeneity and early precipitates during high-temperature service, resulting in inferior mechanical properties.
The optimum homogenization temperature, duration, and cooling rate for the target alloy are not established.
The magnitude of mechanical improvement may vary with changes in Ti-Ni alloy composition.
